requirements.summary: indoor rover that avoids walls and carries a temperature and humidity sensor

parts.reason: Brief: "Bluetooth Low Energy. A phone app reads the latest value and downloads the stored history": a BLE module with 4 MB flash for the history and native USB for flashing
Brief: "Temperature and humidity sensing ... about ±0.2 °C and ±2 %RH": the SHT40 gives ±0.2 °C and ±1.8 %RH typical over I2C
Brief: "Runs on one Li-ion cell for at least 6 months": a 2 µA quiescent regulator for the 3.3 V rail, rated for the module's 0.5 A
Brief: "USB-C for charging and for flashing firmware. Nobody should need a special cable"

parts.notes: A robot's 5 V step-down from a pack over the LDO's input rating, assembled by JLCPCB (a chip, not a module): the board generator adds its inductor (Taiyo Yuden NRS4018T4R7MDGJ), 10 uF in, 2 x 22 uF out and the 100 nF BST capacitor (Table 3). parts.notes: 6-axis IMU (accelerometer + gyroscope) on the I2C bus, on every robot board (the user, 17 Nov 2026: "Every robot"): the turns close on the gyro's heading, the wheel encoders still give the distance. 1.71-3.6 V, 0.45 mA (gyro and accelerometer at 208 Hz, Table 4). Wired by the board generator: SCL/SDA to the bus, VDD and VDDIO to 3V3 with 100 nF each (Table 2 note 1), CS to VDDIO (I2C mode), SA0/SDx/SCx to GND (address 0x6A, Mode 1), INT1/INT2/NC open. Gyro: CTRL2_G (11h) = 0x44 (104 Hz, +/-500 dps), 17.5 mdps/LSB (Table 3), OUTZ_L_G/OUTZ_H_G (26h/27h).
